nodes.namow_test.text.t: The soldier sizes you up with the look of a man who's seen it all twice, and worse the second time.

nodes.odmowa.text.t: "You talk like the ones who sent me here. Smooth, and empty." The soldier blows pipe smoke straight in your face. "Off you go, lad. Come back when you've got more than words."

nodes.po.text.t: "I'm gathering men from the woods. Slow going, because a soldier doesn't like going back where he's been. But they'll come. When you call, they come."

nodes.powitanie.options.[namow].text.t: Try to talk him into helping.

nodes.powitanie.options.[zaufanie].text.t: Wojmir said the army remembers its own.

nodes.powitanie.text.t: An old soldier sits by the Watchtower gate, staring at nothing. "What? I'm not receiving anyone. The Watchtower's been shut two years, and me longer still."

nodes.prowiant.text.t: The soldier takes the two bundles and presses them to his chest with the dignity of a hetman. "Rations. First in three weeks. For that I swear you my loyalty, if loyalty's what I think it is." He smiles crookedly. "My men will come. Just remember, a hungry soldier stays loyal till the first bowl of soup."

nodes.sojusz.text.t: The soldier is silent a long while, then slowly nods. "All right. I'll go with you. Not because you can talk, but because there's no lie in your voice. My men will come when I call. Twelve. Thirteen, if you count the cat." He holds out a hand cracked like dry clay.

nodes.zaufanie.text.t: The soldier raises his head as if he'd heard a familiar horn call. "Wojmir? The one from the tribute party? I knew his father. The old man used to say the army remembers its own. The only words you can trust in this whole Empire." He gets up, slowly, his bones aching. "I'll go with you. For him."
